summary: This note is a wiki-style overview of Brigham Young University (BYU), covering its national rankings, its museums, and its Honor Code. It cites U.S. News & World Report, Forbes, The Princeton Review, and a 2013 Quarterly Journal of Economics study for rankings, and describes the Museum of Art, Museum of Peoples and Cultures, BYU Museum of Paleontology, and Monte L. Bean Life Science Museum. It also explains the history and enforcement of the Honor Code, including the ecclesiastical endorsement requirement and criticism from LGBT advocacy groups.
one_line: Overview of Brigham Young University's rankings, campus museums, and Honor Code history and enforcement.
key_facts: For 2016, U.S. News & World Report ranked Brigham Young University as tied for 66th among national universities in the United States.
A 2013 Quarterly Journal of Economics study ranked BYU No. 21 for where the nation's top high school students choose to enroll.
The Princeton Review ranked BYU the best value for college in 2007.
BYU's library was ranked No. 1 nationally in 2004 and No. 4 in 2007 by a ranking cited in the note.
In 2008-2009 rankings, BYU was ranked No. 1 nationally for students who go on to dental school.
Forbes Magazine ranked BYU as the No. 1 "Top University to Work For in 2014" and as the best college in Utah.
BYU is designated as a research university with high research activity by the Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching.
The Museum of Peoples and Cultures is a museum of archaeology and ethnology with more than 40,000 artifacts and 50,000 photographs.
The BYU Museum of Paleontology was built in 1976 to display fossils found by Dr. James A. Jensen and holds artifacts from the Jurassic Period (210-140 million years ago).
The BYU Museum of Paleontology receives about 25,000 visitors every year.
The Monte L. Bean Life Science Museum was formed in 1978 and features plant and animal life for research by students and scholars.
The Honor Code itself was not created until about 1940 and was used mainly for cases of cheating and academic dishonesty.
President Wilkinson expanded the Honor Code in 1957 to include other school standards.

Karl G. Maeser created the "Domestic Organization", a group of teachers who visited students at their homes to check compliance with rules against obscenity, profanity, smoking, and alcohol consumption.
Both LDS and non-LDS students are required to meet annually with a Church leader to receive an ecclesiastical endorsement for acceptance and continuance.
The Princeton Review ranked BYU as the 3rd most LGBT-unfriendly school in the United States.
